pages.intro: `MfxClient` is the one object an application makes: it signs every request with the API key's Ed25519 private key and holds a namespace for each part of the API (`client.terminals`, `client.execution`, `client.tradingAccounts` and the rest). A list is read a `Page` at a time, or as an async iterator that follows the cursor.

pages.intro: `client.terminals` asks for hosted trading terminals, lists them, waits for one to be usable, reads its journal and restarts many at once.

types.name: Terminal
types.doc: A terminal, as the API describes it.

types.name: TerminalState
types.doc: The states a terminal moves through. Only ACTIVE can be used; see [isUsable](#terminals.isUsable).

types.name: Redundancy
types.doc: How a terminal is replicated.

types.name: TerminalJournal
types.doc: A terminal's journal: its lines newest first, and whether they were read live.

types.name: JournalLine
types.doc: One line of a terminal's MetaTrader journal.

types.name: JournalOptions
types.doc: What [Terminals.journal](#terminals.Terminals.journal) takes.

members.name: lines
members.doc: How many lines, newest first: 1 to 200. The platform's default is 100.

types.name: TerminalFilter
types.doc: Narrow a terminal list in the query, before the page is cut.

members.name: labels
members.doc: Only terminals carrying every one of these labels, by exact key and value. At most 10.

members.name: state
members.doc: Only terminals in one of these states.

types.name: CreateTerminal
types.doc: What [Terminals.create](#terminals.Terminals.create) takes.

members.name: brokerId
members.doc: The broker, from the catalogue.

members.name: serverId
members.doc: The broker's server the terminal logs in to.

members.name: idempotencyKey
members.doc: Required: the same key sent again returns the same terminal, not a second one.

members.name: farmId
members.doc: Leave it out and the platform chooses a farm; the one it chose is on the answer.

members.name: instruments
members.doc: The broker's own symbol names (`EURUSD.sd`).

types.name: PageOptions
types.doc: What [Terminals.page](#terminals.Terminals.page) takes.

members.name: cursor
members.doc: The `nextCursor` of the page before; leave it out for the first page.

members.name: limit
members.doc: How many to a page, 1 to 200.

types.name: isUsable
types.doc:
Can this terminal be used right now: market data, execution, account reads? True only in ACTIVE.
OFFLINE means its host is not reporting; the platform brings it back by itself, so retry rather
than create another. QUEUED means it is placed and waiting for its turn to start: its host
starts terminals a few at a time, and `queue.expected_start_at` says when to expect it.

types.name: TerminalQueue
types.doc: Where a QUEUED terminal waits: its place, its expected start and why it waits.

types.name: BulkAction
types.doc: A bulk restart: what was taken, what was refused, and its expected finish.

types.name: WaitOptions
types.doc: What [Terminals.waitUntilActive](#terminals.Terminals.waitUntilActive) takes.

members.name: timeoutMs
members.doc: How long to wait in all, in milliseconds. 15 minutes unless given.

types.name: BulkAsk
types.doc: Which of your terminals a bulk action takes, and why. At least one filter.

members.name: reason
members.doc: Why; written to the audit log and to each item.

members.name: idempotencyKey
members.doc: Required: the same key sent again returns the same action.

members.name: confirmOpenPositions
members.doc: Without it, a terminal with open positions is refused and the rest are taken.

types.name: Terminals
types.doc: Provision and inspect the terminals this key's tenant owns.

members.name: get
members.doc: One terminal: its state, since when, and its observed conditions. Another tenant's is 404.

members.name: page
members.doc: One page of this tenant's terminals, newest first. One request.

members.name: list
members.doc:
Every terminal, following the cursor, one request a page. There is no total. `labels` and
`state` narrow the list on the platform, so a filtered page is never short for being filtered.

members.name: journal
members.doc:
The terminal's MetaTrader journal, newest first. While it runs the lines are read from its
host (`from: "live"`); after it stops they are the last lines its host kept, for 24 hours
(`from: "last_words"`). Account numbers are masked. A terminal with no lines held is 409.

members.name: create
members.doc:
Ask for a terminal. Answered at once in state REQUESTED; the move to a host happens after.
Sent once and never retried: if the answer is lost, send the same idempotency key again.

members.name: waitUntilActive
members.doc:
Read the terminal until it is no longer on its way to ACTIVE (REQUESTED, QUEUED, PROVISIONING,
LOGGING_IN), or until `timeoutMs` has been waited. Returns the last read either way: ACTIVE,
a state it settled in instead (FAILED, for one), or still on its way when the time ran out.

A QUEUED terminal is read again at its `queue.expected_start_at` (between 2 s and a minute
away), not on a fixed beat: its host starts terminals a few at a time, so asking every two
seconds tells nothing new. Any other state is read again after 2 s, doubling to 15 s.

members.name: bulkRestart
members.doc:
Restart many of your terminals at once. Each is judged by the rules of a single restart; a
refused one is listed in `refused` with its rule's code and the rest are taken. Each host
carries its share at its own pace, so the terminals already running on it are not slowed.
Answered at once with the action and its expected finish; its items never expire.

members.name: getBulkAction
members.doc: A bulk action's progress: counts per state, what was refused, and its expected finish.

members.name: cancelBulkAction
members.signature: cancelBulkAction(bulkActionId: string, options: { readonly idempotencyKey: string }): Promise<BulkAction>
members.doc: Cancel a bulk action: its waiting items are cancelled, running ones finish.

pages.intro: `client.execution` places, changes and cancels orders and changes and closes positions on a terminal. Every method resolves to an `ExecutionResult` and never rejects for anything the platform or the network does; only a wrong argument throws, before anything is sent. The idempotency key is required, nothing is retried automatically, and prices and volumes are decimal strings.

types.name: PlaceOrder
types.doc: What [Execution.placeOrder](#execution.Execution.placeOrder) takes.

members.name: symbol
members.doc: The broker's own symbol name (`EURUSD.sd`); MFX never renames an instrument.

members.name: volume
members.doc: In lots, as a decimal string: `"0.01"`. A number is refused.

members.name: idempotencyKey
members.doc: Required: the same key sent again returns the original command, not a second order.

members.name: orderType
members.doc: `market` unless given.

members.name: price
members.doc: A pending order's price; for `stop_limit`, the stop price where the order wakes up.

members.name: stopLimitPrice
members.doc: For `stop_limit` only: the limit order placed when the stop price is reached.

members.name: deviationPoints
members.doc: How far from the requested price a market order may fill, in points.

members.name: expiresAt
members.doc: When a pending order expires.

members.name: expiresInMs
members.doc: How long the platform may hold the command before it gives up, 1,000 to 60,000 ms.

members.name: magic
members.doc: The expert advisor number the order is tagged with.

members.name: comment
members.doc:
Up to 31 characters, counted in code points (an emoji is one); longer is refused, because the
terminal would cut it without saying so.

types.name: Keyed
types.doc: Every command on an existing order or position takes its key; nothing else is required.

members.name: idempotencyKey
members.doc: Required: the same key sent again returns the original command, not a second one.

types.name: ModifyOrder
types.doc: What [Execution.modifyOrder](#execution.Execution.modifyOrder) takes: only what changes; at least one field.

members.name: expiresAt
members.doc: A new expiry; `null` removes it and the order stays until cancelled.

types.name: ModifyPosition
types.doc: What [Execution.modifyPosition](#execution.Execution.modifyPosition) takes: a stop loss, a take profit, or both.

types.name: ClosePosition
types.doc: What [Execution.closePosition](#execution.Execution.closePosition) takes.

members.name: deviationPoints
members.doc: How far from the price the close may fill, in points; the platform's default is 20.

members.name: comment
members.doc:
The closing deal's comment, up to 31 characters counted in code points; absent, it takes the
position's own.

types.name: ClosePositionPartial
types.doc: What [Execution.closePositionPartial](#execution.Execution.closePositionPartial) takes.

members.name: volume
members.doc: The volume to close, in lots, as a decimal string, inside the symbol's step.

types.name: ClosePositionBy
types.doc: What [Execution.closePositionBy](#execution.Execution.closePositionBy) takes.

members.name: byTicket
members.doc: The opposite position, in the same symbol, that this one is closed against.

types.name: SetTrailingStop
types.doc: What [Execution.setTrailingStop](#execution.Execution.setTrailingStop) takes.

members.name: distance
members.doc: How far behind the best price the stop loss follows, as a price distance: `"0.0020"`.

types.name: WaitFor
types.doc: What [Execution.waitFor](#execution.Execution.waitFor) takes.

members.name: timeoutMs
members.doc: How long to keep reading, 1 ms to 10 minutes; 30 s unless given.

members.name: idempotencyKey
members.doc: Carried into the result only, so a retry can reuse it.

types.name: POLL_FROM_MS
types.doc: The first pause between reads of a command, doubled each time up to [POLL_CAP_MS](#execution.POLL_CAP_MS).

types.name: POLL_CAP_MS
types.doc: The longest pause between two reads of a command.

types.name: Resource
types.doc: Where a command goes: a terminal's routes, or a trading account's on any venue.

types.name: Execution
types.doc: Order entry for one tenant. Every method resolves to a result; none rejects.

members.name: constructor
members.doc:
`resource` is where the commands go: a terminal's routes (`client.execution`) or a trading
account's (`client.tradingAccounts`), which take the same bodies under the same rules.

members.name: placeOrder
members.doc:
Place a market or pending order. Resolves once the platform has persisted the command
(state ACCEPTED, with its `commandId`); the outcome follows on the stream.

Throws only for a wrong argument, before anything is sent: a number where a decimal string
belongs, a missing idempotency key, a comment over 31 characters.

members.name: modifyOrder
members.signature: modifyOrder(terminalId: string, ticket: number, change: ModifyOrder): Promise<ExecutionResult>
members.doc:
Amend a pending order's price, stops or expiry; at least one must change. Its volume, side,
type and symbol cannot be amended: cancel it and place another.

members.name: cancelOrder
members.signature: cancelOrder(terminalId: string, ticket: number, options: Keyed): Promise<ExecutionResult>
members.doc: Cancel a pending order. First class, not a modify with a special case.

members.name: modifyPosition
members.signature: modifyPosition(terminalId: string, ticket: number, change: ModifyPosition): Promise<ExecutionResult>
members.doc: Move a position's stop loss, take profit, or both. At least one is required.

members.name: closePosition
members.signature: closePosition(terminalId: string, ticket: number, options: ClosePosition): Promise<ExecutionResult>
members.doc: Close a position in full.

members.name: closePositionPartial
members.signature: closePositionPartial(terminalId: string, ticket: number, options: ClosePositionPartial): Promise<ExecutionResult>
members.doc: Close part of a position: the volume to close, inside the symbol's step. The rest stays.

members.name: closePositionBy
members.signature: closePositionBy(terminalId: string, ticket: number, options: ClosePositionBy): Promise<ExecutionResult>
members.doc:
Close a position against an opposite one in the same symbol (hedging accounts): the smaller
disappears and the larger is reduced by its volume.

members.name: setTrailingStop
members.signature: setTrailingStop(terminalId: string, ticket: number, options: SetTrailingStop): Promise<ExecutionResult>
members.doc:
Keep the position's stop loss `distance` behind the best price it reaches, only ever tighter.
Setting it again replaces the distance and keeps what the stop has reached.

members.name: clearTrailingStop
members.signature: clearTrailingStop(terminalId: string, ticket: number, options: Keyed): Promise<ExecutionResult>
members.doc: Remove the position's trailing stop. The stop loss stays where the trail left it.

members.name: waitFor
members.doc:
Read the command until it is final, or until `timeoutMs` (30 s unless given), pausing 200 ms
and doubling up to 2 s between reads. Returns the last answer either way: a command still
EXECUTING when the time runs out is reported as it is, not guessed at. **A result that is not
final is never a reason to send again**: an UNKNOWN command may already be a position.

members.name: getCommand
members.doc:
One command and its result, as the platform has it now. A command of another tenant is not
found, never forbidden. Like every method here it resolves to a result and never rejects:
a caller checking what happened to an order must not have to catch to learn it cannot tell.

`idempotencyKey` is only carried into the result, so a retry can reuse it; a read sends none.

types.name: CommandState
types.doc: Where a command is. Final: SUCCEEDED, FAILED, EXPIRED, REJECTED. UNKNOWN is not final.

types.name: Reason
types.doc:
Why a command ended as it did: the platform's reasons, and four the SDK concludes itself
(`transport_error`, `timeout`, `refused`, and `maintenance` when the API refuses outright).
A reason the platform adds later arrives in `reasonText` as it was sent, with `reason` null.

types.name: Tickets
types.doc: The terminal relates one order, one deal and one position per fill; null where none is yet.

types.name: VenueDeal
types.doc:
One deal a command made, as the venue reported it (cTrader): two for an emulated close-by, one
for an order filled at once. `volumeUnits` is in units of the instrument, not lots.

types.name: ExecutionResult
types.doc:
The whole answer to one execution call. Never thrown, always returned.

Read `state` first: SUCCEEDED is done; FAILED, EXPIRED and REJECTED did not happen; UNKNOWN may
already be a position and must never be sent again under a new key.

members.name: ok
members.doc: True when the command succeeded.

members.name: idempotencyKey
members.doc: The key this call was made with, so a retry can reuse it without bookkeeping.

members.name: clientRttMs
members.doc: How long the SDK waited, end to end, in milliseconds. Always known.

members.name: commandId
members.doc: The platform's id for the command.

members.name: final
members.doc: True once the platform will not change this answer again.

members.name: retryable
members.doc: Whether sending the same order again under a NEW key can succeed. False while UNKNOWN.

members.name: duplicate
members.doc: The same key with the same body: this is the original command, not a second one.

members.name: reason
members.doc: Why it ended as it did; null when the platform gives none, as on a success.

members.name: reasonText
members.doc: The reason exactly as it arrived, including one this SDK version does not know.

members.name: mt5Retcode
members.doc: The trading platform's own return code, and its meaning in words.

members.name: commentRaw
members.doc: The broker's own comment, verbatim.

members.name: terminalState
members.doc: The terminal's state when the command was answered.

members.name: execPrice
members.doc: The price and volume the broker filled at, as decimal strings.

members.name: attempts
members.doc: How many times the platform sent it to the broker.

members.name: reroutedFrom
members.doc: The terminal a failover moved this command from, when one did.

members.name: detail
members.doc: What the platform or the SDK said when the request was refused outright.

members.name: retryAt
members.doc: When sending it again can work: a maintenance window's end, where the platform said.

members.name: venue
members.doc: The venue that answered, `mt5` or `ctrader`; null until there is a result.

members.name: venueCode
members.doc:
The venue's own code for a refusal, verbatim, beside `reason` (cTrader: such as
NOT_ENOUGH_MONEY). Null on a terminal, whose code is `mt5Retcode`.

members.name: deals
members.doc: Every deal the command made, in order (cTrader). Empty on a terminal, where `tickets.deal` is it.

members.name: volumeUnits
members.doc: The volume filled in units of the instrument; `execVolume` stays in lots. Null on a terminal.

members.name: closeByEmulated
members.doc: A close-by the venue has no equivalent for, done as two closes (cTrader).

members.name: protectionNotSet
members.doc: A market order filled but its stop loss or take profit could not be set: it is open without.

pages.intro: `client.tradingAccounts` reads and trades a trading account on any venue: a terminal's account or a cTrader account, by the account's id. It also connects cTrader accounts through a grant.

types.name: Venue

types.name: AccountState

types.name: AccountEnvironment

types.name: TradingSymbolList

types.name: TradingSymbol

types.name: TradingAccountFilter
types.doc: Narrow the list on the platform, before the page is cut.

members.doc: Only accounts on this venue, or on one of these.

members.name: environment
members.doc: Only live, or only demo, accounts.

members.name: state
members.doc: Only accounts in this state, or in one of these.

types.name: TradingAccountPageOptions
types.doc: What [TradingAccounts.page](#trading-accounts.TradingAccounts.page) takes.

members.name: cursor
members.doc: The `nextCursor` of the page before; leave it out for the first page.

members.name: limit
members.doc: How many to a page, 1 to 200.

types.name: TradingAccounts
types.doc: Read, trade and connect the trading accounts this key's tenant holds.

members.name: get
members.doc:
One trading account, by its own id or by one of its terminals' ids. Another tenant's, or an id
that is not an account of yours, is 404.

members.name: page
members.doc: One page of this tenant's trading accounts, newest first. One request.

members.name: list
members.doc:
Every trading account, following the cursor, one request a page. There is no total. The
filters narrow the list on the platform, so a filtered page is never short for being filtered.

members.name: funds
members.doc:
Balance, equity, margin and profile, answered by the account's lead runner. On cTrader the
equity is computed by the platform (the venue sends none); `stale` says when it could not be.

members.name: positions
members.doc: Every open position, as one snapshot. On cTrader `volume` is in lots.

members.name: pendingOrders
members.doc: Every pending order, as one snapshot.

members.name: dealsPage
members.doc:
One page of deals inside a window of at most 31 days, newest first, optionally of one
position. On cTrader every time is UTC and `magic` is the order's origin marker.

members.signature: deals(accountId: string, window: DealWindow): AsyncGenerator<Deal, void, undefined>
members.doc: Every deal inside the window, following the cursor, one request a page.

bars are Spotware's trendbars for the account's own symbol name, in UTC; when the window
holds more than `limit` the answer is the newest of them, and the forming bar is included

(`not_on_this_venue`). No bar in the window is an empty list.

types.name: BillingPaymentRequiredError
types.doc:
402 `billing_payment_required`: a payment is missing on the billing profile the request falls
under, and nothing was done.

It is **not retryable**: sending the same request again changes nothing until the payment is
made. At `stage` `reminder` it comes only from a request that adds something billed (a new
account, an add-on switched on). Once `stage` is `suspended` it can come from **any write** on
the tenant or the profile (orders, account changes, copy settings), whatever route it was sent
to, not only the routes that document it. **Reads keep working** throughout, the billing reads
(`client.billing`) included.

What a caller does: show `message` and [action](#errors.BillingPaymentRequiredError.action) to a person. `action.portalPath` is the
portal page where they fix it (a top-up, or the invoice to pay). Once paid, the accounts are
released, usually within the hour; then send the request again (a write under the same
idempotency key). `payBy` is the last moment a payment avoids the suspension that begins at
`suspendsAt`.

Execution methods never throw: an order refused for billing comes back as a refused
`ExecutionResult` whose `detail` carries this error's message.

Every detail is read from `details`, and is null where the platform did not say or wrote
something that cannot be read.

members.doc: The tenant the refusal concerns.

members.doc: The billing profile the request falls under; on Standard, its one profile.

members.name: stage
members.doc:
`reminder` (only what adds something billed is refused) or `suspended` (every write on the
profile's accounts is). Read a word you do not know as text.

types.name: TermsNotAcceptedError
types.doc:
409 `terms_not_accepted`: a version of the Terms of Service or the MetaTrader 5 licence the
organisation must accept is past its grace period, and nobody has accepted it. Not retryable
unchanged.

Adding a terminal and attaching an expert advisor are refused until an owner or admin accepts
it in the customer portal; nothing running is touched, and reads, orders and positions keep
working. [documents](#errors.TermsNotAcceptedError.documents) names each document, its version and when its grace period ended.

members.name: documents
members.doc: Each document due, from `details.documents`; empty if the platform named none.

types.name: ServiceAgreementNotAcceptedError
types.doc:
409 `service_agreement_not_accepted`: the organisation is moving to another plan and the new
plan's Service Agreement has not been accepted, or a version of its plan's Service Agreement
that must be accepted is past its grace period. Not retryable unchanged.

Until an owner or admin accepts it at [acceptUrl](#errors.ServiceAgreementNotAcceptedError.acceptUrl), adding a terminal, attaching an expert
advisor, generating or replacing an API key and asking for higher limits are refused. Nothing
running is touched: reads, orders, positions, detach, stop, restart and resume all keep
working. Where the Terms are held as well, this is the error, and [documents](#errors.ServiceAgreementNotAcceptedError.documents) lists every
document due. `client.tenant.serviceAgreement()` says what is due at any time.

Every detail is read from `details`, and is null (or empty) where the platform did not say or
wrote something that cannot be read.

members.doc: The plan change awaiting acceptance; null when none is (a version past its grace period).

members.name: documents
members.doc: Each document due, the Terms included when they are held too; empty if none was named.

members.name: acceptUrl
members.doc: Where an owner or admin accepts, in the customer portal.
